answer_text: Profit records revenue and costs when they are earned or incurred, whereas cash flow records when money is actually received or paid. The £45,000 credit sales may increase April profit, but customers will not pay for 60 days, so this cash is not available in April. However, Mersey Homeware must pay suppliers £31,000 after 30 days. Therefore, it may have a cash timing gap: £0 received from these credit sales in April − £31,000 paid to suppliers = −£31,000. It can therefore report a £28,000 profit while lacking enough cash to meet payments.
